statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-27139 (GO-2026-4602): on Unix, File.ReadDir and File.Readdir on a directory opened through an os.Root could return FileInfo for a file outside the root, exposing lstat metadata from arbitrary locations. It is fixed in Go 1.25.8 and 1.26.1: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-4602, https://go.dev/issue/77827, https://go.dev/cl/749480, https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/EdhZqrQ98hk. Read every published alertmanager-fips package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine security repository, where the FIPS packages are published: 36 builds, 0.31.1-r0 to 0.35.0-r2, each for x86_64 and aarch64, each verified against the checksum in the package index; the alertmanager-fips-dev packages built from the same source were read too and hold the same two programs from the same toolchains. Each package installs two files, /usr/bin/alertmanager and /usr/bin/amtool, Go programs built with CGO_ENABLED=0 and with the Go Cryptographic Module (GOFIPS140=v1.0.0-c2097c7c). Both programs in a build use the same Go toolchain, read from their Go build information: go1.25.7 in 0.31.1-r0, inside the affected range; go1.26.1 or later in every build from 0.31.1-r1 on (go1.26.1 in 0.31.1-r1 to 0.31.1-r4; go1.26.2 in 0.31.1-r5 to 0.32.1-r0; go1.26.3 in 0.32.1-r1 and 0.32.1-r2; go1.26.4 in 0.32.1-r3 to 0.33.1-r0; go1.26.5 in 0.33.1-r1 to 0.33.1-r3; go1.26.6 in 0.33.1-r5 and 0.34.0-r0; go1.26.7 in 0.34.0-r1; go1.26.8 in 0.34.0-r2 to 0.34.1-r1; go1.26.9 in 0.34.1-r2 and 0.34.1-r3; go1.26.10 in 0.34.1-r4 to 0.35.0-r0; go1.26.11 in 0.35.0-r1 and 0.35.0-r2). The programs are built without a symbol table, so functions were read from each binary's Go function table (pclntab), which lists runtime.main in every binary. The Go vulnerability database names os.OpenInRoot, Root.Open, Root.ReadFile and the rootFS Open, ReadDir and ReadFile methods for this advisory. None of them is listed in either program in 0.31.1-r0 to 0.33.1-r3, which includes 0.31.1-r0, the only build with an affected Go release; from 0.33.1-r5 on both programs list os.(*Root).ReadFile, and all of those builds use go1.26.6 or later, which carry the fix. A strings search, which also finds the names of inlined functions, agrees on the 0.31.1-r0, 0.31.1-r1, 0.33.1-r3, 0.33.1-r5 and 0.35.0-r2 x86_64 alertmanager and the 0.31.1-r0, 0.31.1-r1, 0.33.1-r3 and 0.33.1-r5 aarch64 alertmanager-fips packages: no os.Root or rootFS names before 0.33.1-r5, and os.(*Root).Open and os.(*Root).ReadFile from 0.33.1-r5 on. Because those functions are linked in builds from 0.33.1-r5 on, the status follows the Go release rather than the absence of the functions in earlier builds. The range ends at 0.31.1-r1, so 0.31.1-r0 reads as affected even though it does not link these functions.

statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-27139 (GO-2026-4602): on Unix, File.ReadDir and File.Readdir on a directory opened through an os.Root could return a FileInfo describing a file outside the root, leaking lstat metadata. It is fixed in Go 1.25.8 and 1.26.1: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-4602, https://go.dev/issue/77827, https://go.dev/cl/749480, https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/EdhZqrQ98hk. Go 1.25.8 carries the fix as https://github.com/golang/go/commit/4091800393d254befde3770fd16f51200ebd5a3d on release-branch.go1.25, which names CVE-2026-27139. The escape needs a directory opened through an os.Root, and the advisory lists the os.Root entry points OpenInRoot, Root.Open, Root.ReadFile and the Root file system's Open, ReadDir and ReadFile. We read the Go build information and the Go function table (pclntab) of every Go program in every published build-fips package in the authenticated DHI Alpine 3.23 security repository, where the FIPS packages are published, x86_64 and aarch64: 91 versions from 2.6.4-r0 to 2.30.0-r0, with 2.6.4-r0 published for aarch64 only, each package verified against the index checksum. 2.19.1-r1 is listed three times per architecture with different checksums; the copy the repository serves was the one read. The Go programs are /usr/bin/build, from 2.26.2-r1 also /opt/docker/dhi/yq, and from 2.28.0-r1 also /usr/bin/dhi-source; from 2.27.1-r1 the packages also carry /opt/docker/dhi/uv, a Rust program with no Go function table. No package contains a symbolic link. No Go program in any of these builds has a function of os.Root in its function table: none of the advisory's listed functions, and no other os function whose name contains Root. A byte search of every ELF file in every build also finds none of the names os.(*Root), os.OpenInRoot, os.OpenRoot, os.rootFS, os.openRootNolog or os.rootOpenFileNolog, which also covers inlined functions. Every Go program does contain runtime.main and os.(*File).ReadDir, which we used as controls for both searches. File.ReadDir and File.Readdir are linked and in the builds before 2.7.0-r1 are the unfixed Go 1.25.7 versions, but without os.Root code no directory in these programs can be opened through a Root, so the escape cannot occur. As a positive control, the same function-table reader and byte search run on a program we built with Go 1.25.7 for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 that calls os.OpenInRoot, os.OpenRoot, Root.Open, Root.ReadFile and the Root file system find os.OpenInRoot, os.(*Root).ReadFile, os.(*rootFS).Open, os.(*rootFS).ReadDir and os.(*rootFS).ReadFile in the function table and the os.(*Root) name in the bytes. All Go programs in one build are compiled with the same Go release: 2.6.4-r0 to 2.6.6-r1 Go 1.25.7; 2.7.0-r1 to 2.8.3-r0 Go 1.25.8; 2.8.3-r1 to 2.9.2-r0 Go 1.26.1; 2.10.0-r0 to 2.15.0-r0 Go 1.26.2; 2.15.0-r1 to 2.17.3-r0 Go 1.26.3; 2.17.3-r1 to 2.20.0-r2 Go 1.26.4; 2.20.0-r3 to 2.20.0-r5 Go 1.26.5; 2.20.0-r6 Go 1.26.6; 2.20.0-r7 to 2.20.0-r10 Go 1.26.7; 2.20.0-r11 to 2.26.0-r0 Go 1.26.8; 2.26.0-r1 to 2.26.1-r0 Go 1.26.9; 2.26.1-r1 to 2.28.0-r2 Go 1.26.10; 2.28.0-r3 to 2.30.0-r0 Go 1.26.11. The vulnerable code is therefore not present in any build.
